name: Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Saksaki
nameAr: إبراهيم بن عبد الرحمن السكسكي، أبو إسماعيل، الكوفي، مولى صخير
diedNote: no death year is recorded in the Taqrib; the Shamela record places it between 111 and 120 AH

students.name: Mis'ar ibn Kidam
students.source: al-Daraqutni as quoted in Hady al-Sari, ch. 8, hadith 42 (Mis'ar's route stops at Abu Burdah)

verdicts.en: His hadith is written down, though he is not that strong.

verdicts.ar: لم أجد له حديثا منكر المتن، وهو إلى الصدق أقرب منه إلى غيره، ويكتب حديثه كما قال النسائي
verdicts.en: I found no hadith of his with an objectionable text; he is closer to truthfulness than to anything else, and his hadith is written down, as al-Nasa'i said.

verdicts.ar: تكلم فيه يحيى بن سعيد … هو ضعيف
verdicts.en: Asked why Muslim left his hadith: Yahya ibn Sa'id criticised him. Asked whether with reason: he is weak.

verdicts.via: Yahya al-Qattan, through Ali ibn al-Madini

verdicts.en: He has two hadith in the Sahih: one from Abdullah ibn Abi Awfa on the revelation of Al Imran 3:77, which is a corroboration of Ibn Mas'ud's hadith; and this one, from Abu Burdah from his father, discussed under al-Daraqutni's criticisms (hadith 42).

dhahabi.source: al-Kashif, as given on the Shamela record

flags.label: Weakest link of hadith 2996
flags.detail: The only narrator of the chain below the top grade. Al-Bukhari has two hadith from him, both supported (Hady al-Sari, ch. 9); Muslim did not use him. Ibn Hajar's defence of hadith 2996 does not rest on him but on the shape of the report and on al-Awwam's preservation of the story.

bio: A Kufan client of the fifth generation, placed by Ibn Hajar in the fifth rank of the Taqrib: truthful but weak in memory. Ahmad called him weak and Shu'bah had reservations, while Ibn Adi found nothing objectionable in his texts and Ibn Hibban listed him among the reliable. Al-Bukhari used him in two places only, each with support.

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 9, letter alif (Wikisource)
